Author: Manoj Kumar Gupta
Bench: Manoj Kumar Gupta
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:74245-Db

Petitioner :- Mohit Shukla And 2 Others

Counsel for Petitioner :- Shraddha Shukla

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.
1.

Heard Sri Narendra Kumar Goswami for the petitioners, Sri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel, for respondent nos. 1 and 3 and Sri Amit Saxena, learned Senior Counsel, assisted by Sri Vinayak Nath Singh, for respondent no. 2.
2.

The petitioners have prayed for quashing of a demolition notice dated 7.3.2025 and similar notices (not filed) allegedly issued to recorded owners or residents of Jahangeerpur Khadar, based on notification dated 21.7.2009 and for a direction to respondent no. 2 to process the applications Mohit Shukla And 2 Others vs State Of Uttar Pradeh And 2 Others on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111063356/
1 for regularization of constructions under the provisions of the Rural Abadi Sites (Management and Regularization) Regulations, 2011 and to provide rehabilitation to the petitioners as per provisions of Section 96 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and other ancillary reliefs.

entities.text: Mohit Shukla And 2 Others vs State Of Uttar Pradeh And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The impugned notice dated 7.3.2025 is addressed to one Vijay Kumar Sharma and thereby he has been called upon to stop constructions being undertaken without any permission and to remove illegal constructions over Plot No. 63, Khasra No. 281M, area 3.0680 hectare, Village Jahangeerpur Khadar, Pargana and Tehsil Mat, District Mathura.
It is stated that the constructions being raised without valid permission was adversely affecting the planned development of the area.
The notice purports to be under Section 10 of the U.P. Industrial Area Development Act, 1976.

The noticee has been directed to remove the offending constructions, or in the alternative, appear before the Authority on 21.3.2025 with his explanation as to why the offending constructions should not be demolished.

4. Sri Amit Saxena, learned Senior Counsel, appearing on behalf of respondent no. 2, submits that no reply has been given in response to the impugned notice and that next date fixed is 9th May,
2025.

He further submits that the notice is not in the name of the petitioners and therefore, the petitioners have no locus to challenge the same and also that the petitioners who have presumably filed the instant petition on behalf of 61 other persons, cannot represent them, as the cause of action, if any, was individual to the person affected.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are claiming title over the land covered by the notice on basis of series of transfers made through sale deeds, gift deeds, etc., by the original tenure holders and their vendees.
The impugned notice is in name of their predecessor-in-interest.
6. It is not disputed before us that the impugned demolition notice is not addressed to the petitioners.

In case the petitioners claim that the offending structure belongs to them on basis of the transfer made by the original tenure holders, it is open to the petitioners to file objection against the impugned notice and in which event, respondent no. 2 will be obliged to decide the same in accordance with law.
However, no ground is made out to quash the impugned notice which is only in nature of a show cause notice.
7. As regards the relief claimed in the instant petition for other owners or residents of the subject land, the petitioners allege that they have an authorization letter in their favour.
8. An authorization letter may only authorize the petitioners to represent the principal, who has given the authority in favour of the petitioners.

As the demolition proposed is directed against individuals, therefore it is an individual cause of action and unless the individual is before us, we decline to examine their claim on the basis of the alleged authorization in favour of the petitioners.

9. It has been held by a Full Bench of this Court in Syed Wasif Husain Rizvi vs Hasan Raza Khan & 6 Others, reported in AIR 2016 ALLAHABAD 52, that a power of attorney holder cannot maiantain Mohit Shukla And 2 Others vs State Of Uttar Pradeh And 2 Others on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111063356/
2 proceedings in his own name, unless the principal is before the court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. In view of the above, the instant petition, insofar as it purports to be on behalf of other persons in representative capacity, is dismissed with liberty to those persons to avail the remedy in their own individual names.

11. In respect of the petitioners, it is left open to them to respond to the impugned notice if they claim that the constructions belong to them and in which event, the reply as may be submitted by the petitioners, shall be duly considered before proceeding to take any action against the petitioners.
12.
It is clarified that in case the petitioners fail to submit any reply within a week from today, it shall be open to the Authority to proceed further in the matter in accordance with law.

(Anish Kumar Gupta, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 8.5.2025/Jaideep/-
